title: the sandbox that is a sandbox
intent: The PTC sandbox checks the name of the binding the model asked for and then evaluates the body the model supplied, in a plain let. The whitelist is a list of names, so a form named read can delete a file. The claim ptc-sandbox-restricts-model-code is refuted, and it stays refuted until the body of the form is constrained, not only its name. The real answer is sandbox.el, which needs Emacs 29 and a CI target; until that exists, the boundary is a static analysis of the form: the free symbols of the body must be inside the whitelist, and anything else is refused before a single form is evaluated.
objection: A static analysis of the free symbols of a form is a parser, and parsers have edges: a macro expands, a backquote evaluates, a funcall reaches anything. The check that the body is confined to the whitelist can pass while the body still reaches the host.
refuted_by: A form whose body reaches the host through a path the analysis does not see, run against the boundary. If such a form runs, the boundary is a description and not a boundary, and the wave has not closed.
